coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For When You
Don't Know Why Yet
coverDek: For the days your life feels unlabeled — no clear calling, no finished plan, just you and the waiting room of your own story.

points.hook: Lord, I keep waiting for the invitation that tells me what I'm actually here for.
paragraphs: Father, some days my life reads like a book with no table of contents — just chapters, no sense of where they're headed. I've asked You the same question in a dozen different moods: what am I actually for? Teach me that purpose is rarely handed over in one sentence. It's revealed the way a photograph develops — slowly, in the dark, long before anything is visible to me.
points.verseText: “For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.”

points.hook: I declare: I was not an afterthought. I was a sentence God finished writing before the world began.
paragraphs: I reject the lie that I'm behind schedule on a life only I was ever assigned to live. Before one day of mine was formed, it was already written in Your book — so no comparison, no delay, no detour gets to rewrite what You already ordained. I was planned on purpose, for a purpose, and I say so out loud today.
points.verseText: “Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.”

points.hook: Notice where "I don't know my purpose" actually lives in your body right now.
paragraphs: It's usually not a mystery of the mind — it's a tightness in the chest, a restlessness that won't let you sit still on an ordinary Tuesday. That unease isn't a malfunction; it's information. It's the part of you that already knows you were made for more than survival mode, even before your mind has the language for it. Let yourself feel the ache without rushing to resolve it today — ache is often just purpose, still unnamed.
points.verseText: “Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ.”

points.hook: You don't have to find your purpose alone in a room with the door locked.
paragraphs: Somebody in your church family has already seen a gift in you that you've talked yourself out of believing is real. Purpose is rarely discovered in isolation — it's confirmed in community, spoken over you by people who've watched you long enough to know what you don't yet see in the mirror. Let someone speak into this season with you. Stop trying to graduate from a calling nobody else was ever meant to help you carry.
points.verseText: “But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.”

points.hook: Baby, you don't have to have it all figured out by the deadline you made up in your head.
paragraphs: Mama's praying over you tonight: rest easy, because the God who called Abraham didn't hand him a map, He just said "go," and the going became the purpose. You are allowed to take the next right step without seeing the whole staircase. Sleep in peace — your life isn't behind, it's exactly as far along as grace has carried it, and grace has never once been late.
points.verseText: “By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.”

cta.closingLine: If this spoke to you, let's stay connected.
